name: HBB FULL GENE ANALYSIS (β-THALASSEMIA)
interpretation:
The variant,c.-50A>C, is present in heterozygous state and the disease indication is thalassemia minor.

 
RECOMMENDATIONS
  • Genetic counseling is recommended.
  • Kindly correlate the results with other clinical findings. 
TEST INFORMATION
  • Sanger testing and analysis was performed only for the exons and exon-intron boundaries in the HBB gene.
  • This test is designed to detect mutations in the above-mentioned regions only. 
  • Extremely rare de novo variants, certain promoter and rare intronic mutations may not be assessed. 
  • This assay does not detect any deletion or duplication except that mentioned in the test description.  
  • Unless reported or predicted to cause disease, alterations found that do not result in an amino acid substitution are  not  reported. These alterations and common polymorphisms identified for this patient will be available upon request.

METHODOLOGY

Sanger sequencing based DNA analysis was performed to identify the mutations in the coding regions and reported mutations in the non-coding regions of β Globin gene (HBB). The 619 bp deletion was carried out by end point PCR (gel electrophoresis). Mutation surveyor software V5.1.1 is used for identifying the mutations and the identified  sequence alterations are reported in accordance with the Human Genome Variants Society (HGVS) nomenclature and annotated using one or more of the following database/s- ClinVar, OMIM, HGMD and SwissVar. 

LIMITATIONS
  • Although all precautions are taken during Molecular Genetic testing the currently available data indicate that the technical error rate for all types of DNA analysis is approximately 2%. 
  • In rare cases because of allele  dropout/large deletions on one allele, heterozygosity may be reported as homozygosity. 
  • Results have been confirmed by bidirectional sequencing, with the error rate of the Taq polymerase for base incorporation being 1 in 6000 bases. 
  • This assay is unable to differentiate between cis and trans mutations.
  • The test has been performed by the laboratory with the assumption that counseling regarding its utility as well as limitations has been conveyed by the referring clinician to the patient/ guardian/family and consent for the same has been obtained after relevant pre-test counseling.
References
